weather_info.climate_type: Hot, semi-arid to arid climate typical of interior Sindh
weather_info.avoid_months: May to July (extreme heat, often above 40°C)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild and pleasant, 10-24°C, best time to visit
Occasional heavy rain, humid, risk of flooding in low areas

travel_tips.tip: Visit Ghotki in the cooler months (November to February) for the most comfortable travel experience.
Intercity buses and shared vans (Suzuki/coaster) are the most common way to reach and travel around the district.
As with most small-town travel in Sindh, arrange accommodation and local guides in advance, especially outside the main town center.

history.founded: Developed as a railway and agricultural town along the Sindh-Punjab border
history.city_history: Ghotki became a separate district in 1993, split from Sukkur district. It sits along the Indus River and the national highway/rail corridor connecting Sindh to Punjab.
history.province_history: Sindh is home to one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro), and was later ruled by Persian, Arab, and Mughal empires, as well as the Talpur dynasty, before British annexation in 1843 and eventual inclusion in Pakistan in 1947.
